name: Bangiomorpha
habitat: Rocky shore of a shallow sea
fact: A red seaweed about 1.05 billion years old — the oldest seaweed we can match to a group alive today. Its threads made different kinds of spore, as red seaweeds that reproduce with male and female forms do today: perhaps the oldest known sex.
debate: Whether its spores really mean sex is argued over; living red seaweeds that look like it do reproduce that way.
sites: Hunting Formation, Somerset Island, Arctic Canada

name: Torridon lake microbes
fact: Microscopic cells, some with ornate walls, preserved in the mud of lakes about a billion years old in north-west Scotland — the first known life away from the sea.
